author: Edge
text:
Clean orders are exactly that. Where there has been no retrace to pick
 them up. Be careful, in some instances what looks clean may not be. For
 example a big pole down which looks like it has left clean orders at a
decision above, may have retraced. So get all the info possible in LTFs

To think about clean orders, turn your mind to CP. True CP (not stacked)
 acts as a pole on the opposing move because any orders have been picked
 up (for reasons discussed all over RTM).

Also, a flag may look completed in one scale, but there are often more
MPLs on tiny scales. One must adjust analysis and expectations for this

author: dengaima
text:
Here is my take for old Task set by Ifmyante

When i was doing the task, I was lost, but then was thinking of boxes and the way ITs think to catch all stops

I am not sure if I am correct, but seems okay to me :)

My thinking process: Supply was strong move down, therefore to fill up rest of the orders, they need buyers.

In order to do so, they cannot move the market fast, otherwise everyone
will just buy and price shoots too far - REMEMBER: For ITs to buy they
need sellers and vice versa.

Therefore from my graph:

1. I as IT moved the price slowly back up to the supply (with CP) and added SELL orders throughout the CP.

2. As the price reached the previous H & S (QM) level, i let it
stall for a while making them believe I am adding more buy orders

at the same time Sellers see Double Top pattern and are ready to sell.

3. At the supply QM level, I remove my buy orders and price moves down making Sellers jumping on the wagon.

4. I suprise them and push the price back to FO level (There are now
greedy buyers on board, and Double top sellers on board + This last push
 up to FO also invites late buyers as they believe its the start of new
"trend")

I noticed, it was easier to make this chart than reading the chart from MT4 lol... I need more practise:DD

author: Ifmyante
text:
Here's a post from Zee's journal:

zee wrote: I really thought that this one was one very decent PA. Apparently not. Comments are welcome.

It really did look like good PA.

But it seems whoever's dropping the Yen through its range is in a big hurry to get there, and is breaking the rules in doing so.

We read PA, and use it extensively for our trading. But the market is
moved by people. Most of these people we see over and over again, making
 plays from the same book all week long.

Sometimes though, a new player will dump a ton of orders into the
market; more than the ITs are willing to cover, and a level will break.

Sometimes an IT will himself make a slip and accidentally break a level.

Sometimes an IT will break a level just to mess with us lot's brains.

These events are extremely rare, but they do happen.

If they didn't happen, we could go all in on every trade, and soon find ourselves as rich as the Rothschilds!

It's due to this risk of false PA that we only risk a small percent of our accounts on any trade or set of correlated trades.

Note: Should the ITs ever change their rulebook, don't worry. I'll have it reverse engineered in no time
